items.title: The Pentagon wants $30 million to build an AI-powered lie detector
items.summary: The US government wants to spend $30.3 million over the next five years on an improved form of lie detector, according to a Department of Defense budget request . The program, called Polygraph+ or Polygraph Next, will focus on scoring algorithms that use artificial intelligence and machine learning and on a technique called “standoff sensing,” which refers to the ability to take physiological readings without attaching a device to a subject’s person. According to details of the budget document, which were first reported by Inside Defense , the project will “modernize federal polygraph and credibility assessment technologies” to improve their accuracy and reliability.
